title: Primary Cytoreductive Surgery & Residual Disease Status (R0)
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology 11e Ch 85
ESGO Advanced Ovarian Cancer Surgery Guidelines

steps.say: Primary surgical debulking aims to eradicate all macroscopically evident peritoneal tumor implants. The prognostic benefit of cytoreduction is directly proportional to the residual disease volume.
steps.tx: The central oncological goal of **primary cytoreduction** is achieving **complete resection (R0)** with **zero gross residual disease** (residual disease **0** mm). This surgical endpoint functions as the single most powerful **survival predictor** in advanced ovarian carcinoma, conferring marked prolongation in progression-free and overall survival compared to any residual disease.

vis.alt: Advanced ovarian peritoneal carcinomatosis and cytoreduction goals

steps.say: Surgical residual disease volume is categorized according to strict international cooperative group thresholds. Complete macroscopic clearance yields the greatest therapeutic benefit.
steps.tx: Residual disease is categorized into: **R0 complete** (no macroscopic residual tumor, residual **0** mm), **optimal <=1 cm (R1)** (macroscopic residual deposits <=**1** cm diameter), and **suboptimal >1 cm (R2)** (macroscopic residual deposits >1 cm or residual grade **2**), with prognosis declining progressively across these surgical tiers.

left.title: R0 Complete Resection (Target Standard)
points: Zero macroscopic residual tumor throughout the entire abdomen
Achievable in >75% of patients with extensive upper abdominal surgery

right.title: Optimal (R1) vs Suboptimal (R2) Debulking
points: Optimal R1: residual disease <=1 cm (intermediate survival ~40 months)
Suboptimal R2: residual disease >1 cm (poor survival ~25-30 months)
Predictive scoring directs bulky unresectable cases to neoadjuvant therapy

steps.say: Achieving complete macroscopic clearance in advanced stage disease frequently necessitates radical upper abdominal surgical procedures. Diaphragmatic stripping, splenectomy, and cholecystectomy are commonly required.
steps.tx: Aggressive **upper abdominal debulking** incorporating **diaphragm peritonectomy**, **splenectomy**, distal pancreatectomy, and cholecystectomy elevates the **R0 rate >75%** (over **75** percent) compared to historical rates of **40** percent, overcoming complex peritoneal carcinomatosis in the upper abdomen and significantly extending long-term patient survival.

rows: Clears bulky left upper quadrant tumor
Greater and lesser omentum, burse floor
Clears confluent tumor cake en bloc

steps.say: The randomized LION trial resolved the controversy surrounding routine pelvic and para aortic lymphadenectomy in advanced ovarian cancer. Systematic nodal dissection in clinically negative cases does not prolong survival.
steps.tx: The randomized **LION trial** published by **Harter 2019** (**2019**) proved that **omission of systematic lymphadenectomy in R0** resection with clinically negative nodes did not compromise progression-free or overall survival, while systematic lymphadenectomy caused **increased morbidity** and higher **60**-day postoperative mortality (**3.1** percent vs **0.9** percent).

rows: Significantly lower infection, lymphocele, and death
Omit routine LND in R0 normal nodes
Resect only bulky suspicious lymph nodes
Standard of care confirmed by ESGO/NCCN

steps.say: Pelvic peritoneal tumor infiltration typically engulfs the cul de sac, rectosigmoid junction, and reproductive organs. An en bloc retroperitoneal resection removes these structures in continuity.
steps.tx: Executing a **modified posterior exenteration** with en bloc **rectosigmoid resection** achieves total **cul-de-sac clearance** when pelvic carcinomatosis obliterates the pouch of Douglas. Restoring bowel continuity via a circular stapled **end-to-end anastomosis** safely re-establishes intestinal transit and achieves complete macroscopic pelvic disease clearance without permanent colostomy.

nodes.label: Develop avascular pararectal and paravesical retroperitoneal spaces
Ligate uterine and internal iliac branches; mobilize ureters bilaterally
Transect proximal sigmoid colon above pelvic disease margin
Excise cul-de-sac en bloc with uterus and re-anastomose rectum

steps.say: Laparoscopic assessment prior to formal laparotomy provides an objective score to evaluate surgical resectability. Fagotti's scoring framework reliably predicts the likelihood of achieving complete cytoreduction.
steps.tx: The laparoscopic **Fagotti score** during **predictive laparoscopy** evaluates peritoneal carcinomatosis, diaphragmatic sheets, and mesenteric disease. A **score >=8 suboptimal cutoff** (**8** or higher) identifies a very high likelihood of suboptimal debulking, facilitating accurate **neoadjuvant selection** for neoadjuvant chemotherapy rather than futile open laparotomy.

steps.say: Radical excision of diaphragmatic tumor implants frequently breaches the pleural space. Close coordination with anesthesia ensures proper intraoperative lung re expansion and air evacuation.
steps.tx: Full-thickness **diaphragmatic resection** for invasive diaphragmatic implants necessitates intraoperative communication with anesthesia for lung recruitment maneuvers and active **pleural evacuation** during muscular closure. Placing a temporary chest catheter ensures comprehensive **pneumothorax prevention** and reduces postoperative atelectasis, symptomatic pleural effusion, and pulmonary morbidity.

nodes.label: Mobilize liver by dividing falciform and coronary ligaments
Resect diaphragm peritoneum and involved muscle full-thickness
Coordinate with anesthesia for sustained positive pressure lung inflation
Perform airtight pleural closure over underwater drain to evacuate air

steps.say: Protective intestinal diversion protects low pelvic bowel anastomoses from catastrophic leak. Specific anatomical and clinical criteria mandate temporary stoma creation.
steps.tx: Constructing a protective **loop ileostomy** is indicated following **ultra-low colorectal anastomosis <5-6 cm** (<**5** to **6** cm from anal verge), in patients who have undergone **multiple bowel resections**, or in malnourished patients receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy to prevent catastrophic pelvic anastomotic leakage and peritonitis.
